analyst_view.overall: Early view: Amorim's Milan beat Genoa before the break despite a long injury list (Pavlovic, Tomori, Gabbia, Chukwueze, Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers and keeper Terracciano), and the squad only returns to training on 16 November. They go to Olympiacos in the Europa League four days later. Frosinone lost 1-0 at Cagliari despite 29 shots, top scorer Raimondo went off injured, and Bracaglia serves a one-match ban for five yellow cards.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. That fits both teams: Milan's home games have averaged four goals and Frosinone's away games about 3.4. Bracaglia's ban weakens Frosinone's defence, but Raimondo's injury (eight goals) blunts their attack, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 9.9 corners. Milan's games are the quietest in the league for corners, under seven a game, but Frosinone's are the busiest at over 13, with eight a game for Frosinone away. Milan let opponents have the ball and are happy to defend crosses, so Frosinone should take most of the corners here. That leaves me at the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. I lean lower: Milan's home games have averaged only about 2.6 cards, and Frosinone's pressing has not produced many bookings, at 1.7 a game. The Genoa game, with four Milan bookings, was more heated than usual.

shots.text: The site expects 33.4 shots. I lean lower because Milan's home games have averaged only about 21 shots: they take few shots and score from them, as they did at Genoa with six shots and two goals. Frosinone will shoot a lot, but even so, 33 looks high for a game at San Siro.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Milan's home games average about 8.8, and Frosinone may be without Raimondo, the main finisher in a side that missed chance after chance at Cagliari. Calò is the other Frosinone player who regularly tests keepers.
